audit.intended_rules: Ch. 10 event-materials rule (booth/demo materials reimbursable only when the note names the event AND states budget-owner pre-approval; missing either → deducted) combined with the Ch. 10 peripherals/test-equipment rule (unit price ≥ €100 reimbursable only with an IT Helpdesk ticket number in the note). Also touches Ch. 2 note requirements for commercial invoices and the Ch. 10 FAQ on buyer name not affecting reimbursability.
realism_issues: Minor wrinkle: buyer_company is 'KlangLabs Audio GmbH', not the policy firm Noice & Toit LLP. The Ch. 10 FAQ explicitly permits invoices addressed to another company provided the employee paid and the note explains the purchase, so this is acceptable, but it reads like the employee's own employer rather than a client.
audit.notes: Arithmetic validates cleanly (line items, subtotal, 19% VAT, total, charges list all consistent). No label.json or receipt.jpg present. Leipzig vendor selling acoustic materials and a calibrated Class 2 sound meter to an audio buyer is plausible; prices are realistic; 2024-04-18 is a Thursday (commercial invoices are never weekend expenses per Ch. 9); German VAT rate and DE tax IDs check out. Adjudication: the note names the purpose (podcast and client demo booth) but states no budget-owner pre-approval, so the foam tiles (239.96), mounting tape (33.80), and isolation pads (47.70) are deducted as event materials missing a required note statement. The sound level meter (145.50) is specialist test equipment at a unit price ≥ €100 with no IT Helpdesk ticket cited, so it is deducted too. Nothing remains: the line is rejected at €0.00 reimbursed. Correct citations: Ch. 10 event-materials card (both statements required), Ch. 10 high-value peripheral/test-equipment card, Ch. 2 calculation steps. Fits subtle_multi well: an agent must combine the event-material pre-approval requirement with the IT-ticket threshold rule, and neither alone is obvious from the plausible-looking note. Keep as-is; a label.json still needs to be authored for this case.

problems: Minor adjudication wrinkle, non-blocking: mounting tape (33.80) and pads (47.70) could alternatively be read as booth/event materials lacking stated pre-approval (fully deducted) rather than incidental consumables capped at EUR 50.00 per invoice (Ch10 'Purchase minor emergency supplies'); either reading still relies on the same two core passages, so the subtle_multi classification holds.
No label.json present for this case, so label consistency could not be checked (optional field, not a defect).
